cards.explanation: The answer is an altar. Jeshua son of Jozadak, a priest, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel began to build the altar of the God of Israel. They did it to sacrifice burnt offerings on it, "…as it is written in the Law of Moses the man of God." So the first thing going up is the place where the offerings will go. I like a crew that starts with what matters most, friends.

The word is "feared." They set up the altar and sacrificed burnt offerings on it, both morning and evening, "…even though they feared the people of the land." The fear is there, and so are the offerings. The text doesn't say the fear went away, only that they kept offering anyway.

The feast is the Feast of Tabernacles. The people "…celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles in accordance with what is written…" They weren't making up a holiday on the spot. They followed what was already written down.

The answer is True. The text says they offered burnt offerings daily, "…based on the number prescribed for each day." Nobody was winging it with the count. They followed what was written for every single day of the feast.

The answer is False. The verse says the offerings began "…although the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not been laid." So the offerings were already going while the foundation was not yet laid. Offerings first, foundation later.
The answer is sea, friends. They gave food and drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So the plan was to ship the wood across the water.
The answer is False. The logs were to be brought "…as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia." The Israelites weren't going around the king. They had his go-ahead for the shipment.

The answer is Levites twenty years old and up. The text says they appointed Levites twenty years of age or older to supervise the construction of the house of the LORD. Then Jeshua, Kadmiel, the sons of Henadad and their families joined together to supervise the workers. All of them were Levites.

They are there to praise the LORD. The priests with trumpets and the Levites with cymbals took their positions "…to praise the LORD…" The text says it was as David king of Israel had prescribed. A foundation was in, and the music was ready.

The word is "shout." "Then all the people gave a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid." It came right after the song, "For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever." The whole crowd joined in.

The ones who wept are the older leaders who saw the first temple, friends. The text says "…many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads who had seen the first temple wept loudly when they saw the foundation of this temple." The text doesn't tell us exactly why they wept. I think those tears carried a lot, and I'll leave it at that.
The answer is True, friends. The text says the older ones wept loudly. Then it adds, "Still, many others shouted joyfully." So the crowd had both sounds going at once, at the same foundation.

The people can't tell the shouts of joy from the weeping. The text says "The people could not distinguish the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, because the people were making so much noise." Joyful shouts and loud weeping were so mixed together that nobody could sort them out. That's a loud crowd.

The answer is True, friends. The last line says, "And the sound was heard from afar." Verse 13 says the people were making so much noise that no one could tell the shouts of joy from the weeping. That's a sound that carried.
